findings.issue: When sudo cannot start, A-2 asks for a single ::warning:: line naming the reason. Recovery reuses runCommand, which prints `::error::apt-lock: could not start sudo -n dpkg --configure -a: ...` (an error annotation on a run that may pass) and resolves 1. The warning then says `(exit code 1)`, which is not the real reason.
findings.evidence: runCommand (apt-lock.js:177-191) logs ::error:: on the 'error' event and resolves 1. main (:266-273) then logs `failed (exit code ${code})`.
findings.fix: Spawn sudo through a small variant that resolves {code, reason} (e.g. `could not start: ENOENT` / `exit code N` / `killed by SIGX`) and logs only the ::warning:: line, or accept the current wording because sudo always exists on hosted runners. In practice this cannot happen there, hence MINOR.

findings.issue: A-6 says the month stamp lets a stale set refresh at most monthly. But the restore-keys prefix restores last month's entry, Restore copies it into /var/cache/apt/archives, and Collect copies everything there back, including superseded versions. So the new month's entry is a superset, and superseded .debs pile up and are never pruned. The set only resets if no prefix entry survives (evicted after 7 days unused).
findings.evidence: Restore: `find ~/.cache/apt-archives ... -exec sudo cp -t /var/cache/apt/archives/ {} +`. Collect: `find /var/cache/apt/archives -maxdepth 1 -name '*.deb' -exec cp -t ~/.cache/apt-archives/ {} +`. Nothing removes .debs that apt no longer references.
findings.fix: Before collecting, run `sudo apt-get autoclean` (it drops archives that can no longer be downloaded) and empty ~/.cache/apt-archives, then copy. Or drop restore-keys so each month starts fresh. This follows the spec as written (spec-level design), so MINOR / follow-up.

findings.issue: `output` containing `ok` also matches the file name `tests/ok.test.ts`, so this assertion would pass even if the test name were missing from the output. exitCode 0 and timedOut false carry the real check.
findings.fix: Assert on something more specific, e.g. /✓ .*ok/ or `1 passed`. The spec wording only requires `ok`, so NIT.

summary: All seven code-verifiable SPEC items (01-07) are implemented as specified, and their tests would fail on a broken implementation. Reverting runInSandbox to spawnSync drops timedOut and leaves the grandchild alive. Dropping the journal check or the ordering breaks the exact marker contents. Missing, misordered or if:-guarded steps fail the static check. The locked workflow.test.ts still passes, and the four relevant files were re-run locally (19/19 green). There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Two MINOR ones: the A-2 wording when sudo cannot start (::error:: plus 'exit code 1'), and stale .debs carried forward by restore-keys (a spec-level design). SPEC-08/09 are manual CI checks for the orchestrator.
